lessons.title: Writing a formal letter
lessons.programRef: MINEDUB primary school curriculum (English-speaking subsystem), Level III (Class 5) — English Language; to be checked against the official syllabus
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Know the layout of a formal letter.
Choose the right greeting and closing.
Write a short polite formal letter.
reviewNotes: Layout conventions vary slightly between textbooks; the model letter is original; check the school's preferred layout.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Layout
blocks.md: A formal letter has: the **writer's address** and the **date** (top right); the **receiver's title and address** (left); the **greeting** (*Dear Sir,* / *Dear Madam,*); a **subject heading** (*REQUEST FOR PERMISSION*); the **body** in short paragraphs; the **closing** (*Yours faithfully,*) and the **name** of the writer.

items.text: I write to ask... Thank you.

blocks.caption: Layout of a formal letter.
blocks.alt: A letter with the writer's address and date at the top right, the headmaster's name on the left, Dear Sir, a heading REQUEST FOR PERMISSION, a short body, Yours faithfully and the name Ako Ndip.

blocks.title: Writing the body
blocks.md: Paragraph 1: **why you write** (*I am writing to ask for permission to ...*). Paragraph 2: the **reason and details**. Paragraph 3: **thanks and hope** (*I hope you will agree. Thank you for your help.*). Use a **polite, formal** tone: no short forms (*do not*, not *don't*), no slang. Use **Yours faithfully** with *Dear Sir/Madam* and **Yours sincerely** with a name.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Using a friendly style: *Hi!* or *Love*.
- Forgetting the subject heading or the date.
- Using *Yours faithfully* with a named person (use *Yours sincerely*).
- Using short forms and slang.

blocks.title: Example 1
steps: We do not know the name of the receiver, so we use the formal closing.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: Write a heading for a letter to the headmaster asking for permission to leave school early.
steps: The heading is short and in capital letters.
REQUEST FOR PERMISSION TO LEAVE SCHOOL EARLY
blocks.answer: REQUEST FOR PERMISSION TO LEAVE SCHOOL EARLY

lessons.title: Composition: narrative and descriptive writing
lessons.programRef: MINEDUB primary school curriculum (English-speaking subsystem), Level III (Class 5) — English Language; to be checked against the official syllabus
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Write a descriptive composition using the senses and good adjectives.
Check your work: spelling, punctuation and tense.
reviewNotes: Word lengths are indicative; the model composition is original.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Narrative composition
blocks.md: Plan before you write: **introduction** (who, where, when), **build-up** (events, the problem), **ending** (solution and lesson). Write in the **past tense**, in **paragraphs**. Use **time words** (*one morning, soon, suddenly, at last*), **direct speech** and strong verbs. Give a **title**. Length: about 150 words at this level.

blocks.caption: The plan of a narrative composition.
blocks.alt: Three boxes: introduction with who, where and when; build-up with events and the problem; ending with the solution and the lesson.

blocks.title: Descriptive composition
blocks.md: To describe a person, an animal, a place or an event, plan what to say about each part: **appearance, sounds, smells, feelings**. Use adjectives, comparisons (*as fast as a motorbike*) and adverbs. Keep a clear order, for example from the entrance to the end of a market.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- No plan, so the story has no clear parts.
- Changing tense or person in the middle.
- A long list of events with no problem and no ending.
- Not checking spelling and punctuation at the end.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: Write an opening paragraph for a story called 'The Storm'.
steps: Say when, where and who, and prepare the problem.
One hot afternoon, Neba was playing football in the yard in Limbe when the sky suddenly turned black.
blocks.answer: One hot afternoon, Neba was playing football in the yard in Limbe when the sky suddenly turned black.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: Write two descriptive sentences about a market using the senses.
steps: See and hear: colours and noises.
The market is full of colourful cloths and loud voices. It smells of fresh fish and roasted corn.
blocks.answer: The market is full of colourful cloths and loud voices. It smells of fresh fish and roasted corn.

exercises.source: Original exercise written for CastBridge, in the style of the curriculum
exercises.prompt: Write a formal letter (about 70 words) to your headmaster asking for permission to attend a family event on Friday. Give your address and the date.
exercises.model:
12 School Road, Buea
5 March 2026

The Headmaster
Government Primary School, Buea

Dear Sir,

REQUEST FOR PERMISSION

I am writing to ask for permission to be absent from school on Friday, 8 March. My cousin's wedding will take place in Bamenda and my parents wish me to attend. I will bring a note from my father. I will copy all the lessons that I miss. Thank you for your kind help.

Yours faithfully,
Ako Ndip
exercises.rubric: Marks (8): addresses and date (2); greeting and closing correct (1); heading (1); reason and polite tone (2); organisation in paragraphs (1); spelling and punctuation (1).

exercises.source: Original exercise written for CastBridge, in the style of the curriculum
exercises.prompt: Write a composition of about 120 words called 'A Day I Will Never Forget'. Use a plan: introduction, build-up and ending.
exercises.model: Last year, on my birthday, my family and I travelled from Bamenda to Limbe to see the sea. We left at six o'clock. Along the way we saw green hills and tea plantations. At the beach I ran toward the waves but I suddenly fell on the wet sand and everyone laughed. Then my father helped me up and we built a big sand castle together. At the end of the day, we ate grilled fish and plantain by the sea. I was tired but very happy. It was the best day of my life.
exercises.rubric: Marks (10): introduction (1); build-up with events (2); ending (1); past tense kept (1); paragraphs (1); varied vocabulary and sentences (2); spelling and punctuation (2).
